tagline: Ford, the steel works, and the hospital insure themselves and handle injured workers’ claims in-house; the small businesses on Michigan Avenue and Warren sometimes carry no coverage at all. The Act gives you 80 percent of your after-tax wage, every medical bill, and a hearing before a magistrate. It also gives you 90 days to report the injury.

c.v: A worker hurt on the job in Dearborn is owed benefits under Michigan’s Workers’ Disability Compensation Act regardless of fault: medical care in full, 80 percent of after-tax wages while unable to work, retraining, and scheduled payments for the loss of a body part. What differs in Dearborn is who is on the other side. Ford, the Rouge complex’s contractors, the steel works, and Corewell Health are self-insured and administer claims through their own adjusters and clinics. The restaurants, bakeries, groceries, and shops along Michigan Avenue and Warren are small employers, some of whom carry no coverage, which changes the claim entirely. And many Dearborn workers report injuries, give statements, and sign forms in a second language, which is where claims are lost before they start.
ATLAW is a personal injury firm at 3 Parklane Boulevard in Dearborn. In 13 years the firm has handled more than 10,000 cases and recovered more than $100 million for clients.

sections.heading: Where Dearborn workers are hurt, and who handles the claim

c.v: The Rouge and Ford.

The Dearborn Truck Plant, Dearborn Stamping, Dearborn Engine, the Rouge Electric Vehicle Center, Ford’s world headquarters and research campus, and the suppliers and logistics operations around them. Repetitive-motion and lifting injuries, crush and amputation injuries from presses and robotics, falls, and exposures. Ford is self-insured; the first 28 days of care are typically at plant medical. The UAW-Ford agreement adds grievance rights and sickness-and-accident benefits that interact with comp (MCL 418.354).
S&A coordination
The steel works and the industrial south.

Cleveland-Cliffs Dearborn Works, the rail and truck yards, and the Rotunda, Oakwood, and Miller Road corridors: burns, crush injuries, falls, and heavy-vehicle strikes. On a multi-employer site the comp claim is against your own employer; the general contractor, other subcontractors, and the property owner are potential third-party defendants, and the MIOSHA file is the first evidence requested.
Corewell Health Dearborn and the clinics.
Patient-handling injuries, needlesticks, assaults by patients, and slips in clinical areas, with the employer’s own occupational health department as the treating clinic.
The City, the schools, and the colleges.

Dearborn Police, Fire, and Public Works; Dearborn Public Schools; Henry Ford College; UM-Dearborn. Public employers with their own pension and duty-disability provisions that run alongside comp and must be coordinated.
City and school coordination; firefighter presumption under 418.405
Michigan Avenue and Warren.

Restaurants, bakeries, groceries, auto repair, and retail: burns, cuts, lifting injuries, and falls in high-turnover workforces where injuries often go unreported past the 90 days. Some of these employers carry no workers’ compensation insurance. An uninsured employer loses the exclusive-remedy protection: the injured worker may claim comp benefits and may also sue the employer in circuit court, and the employer’s officers can be personally liable (MCL 418.641, 418.647).
uninsured-employer remedies
Delivery, rideshare, and logistics.

Drivers hurt in crashes on I-94, Michigan Avenue, and Ford Road while working, which brings Michigan no-fault into the claim (see below). Rideshare drivers are generally independent contractors with no comp claim; see our
Dearborn rideshare page
Temporary, staffing, and undocumented workers.

A worker placed by a staffing agency is the agency’s employee, and the host employer may also be entitled to the exclusive-remedy bar under Michigan’s economic-reality test. Michigan courts have held that medical benefits are owed regardless of immigration status but that wage-loss benefits may be suspended while a worker cannot lawfully accept employment.

sections.heading: What a Dearborn worker is owed

c.v: Medical care

in full, for as long as needed, with no deductible or co-pay (MCL 418.315), including attendant care at home (56 hours a week for family-provided care). For the first 28 days the employer chooses the doctor; after that you may treat with your own physician on notice to the employer (MCL 418.315(1)).
Wage loss

at 80 percent of your after-tax average weekly wage, computed from the highest 39 of the 52 weeks before the injury (MCL 418.351, 418.371), capped at the state maximum; partial wage loss if you return at lower pay (418.361(1)); seven-day waiting period, paid from day one if the disability lasts two weeks (418.311).
Specific loss
for a body part or its use, regardless of wage loss (418.361(2)); total and permanent disability for at least 800 weeks (418.361(3)).
Vocational rehabilitation
up to 52 weeks, extendable to 104 (418.319).
Death benefits
to dependents for 500 weeks plus burial (418.321, 418.345), alongside the third-party wrongful death claim on our
Dearborn wrongful death page

sections.heading: The hearing, and the lawsuit comp does not bar

c.v: When a Dearborn employer or insurer denies a claim or stops paying, the worker files an Application for Mediation or Hearing (Form WC-104A) with the Workers’ Disability Compensation Agency; disputed claims go to mediation and then to a magistrate at the agency’s Detroit hearing office in Cadillac Place, 3026 West Grand Boulevard
, with appeal to the Michigan Compensation Appellate Commission. A contested claim typically takes 12 to 18 months, which is why most disputed claims resolve by
redemption
, a lump-sum settlement approved by the magistrate that closes the claim, including future medical care; do not sign one without advice.

Workers’ compensation is your exclusive remedy against an insured employer (MCL 418.131), but you can sue anyone else whose negligence caused the injury (418.827): the other driver in a crash on the job (with workers’ comp primary and no-fault paying the difference under MCL 500.3109(1); see our

faqs.question: How long do I have to report a work injury in Dearborn?

answer.v: Ninety days from the injury, or from when you knew it was work-related, to notify your employer, and two years to file a claim. Report it in writing the day it happens.

faqs.question: I was hurt at the Rouge. Is the plant’s medical department my only option?

answer.v: For the first 28 days, generally yes. After that you may treat with your own physician on written notice. Your union contract may also provide sickness-and-accident benefits and grievance rights that run alongside the comp claim.

faqs.question: My employer on Warren Avenue has no workers’ comp insurance. What happens?

answer.v: You may still claim comp benefits, and because the employer is uninsured it loses the protection that normally bars a lawsuit: you can sue it in circuit court for your full damages, and its officers can be personally liable. Call immediately.

faqs.question: I was in a crash on I-94 while driving for work. Who pays?

answer.v: Workers’ compensation pays your medical and wage-loss benefits first, your no-fault insurer pays what comp does not cover, and the at-fault driver is liable for pain and suffering if you have a threshold injury. All three claims run at once.
Not if it is insured, except for a deliberate intent to injure. You can sue any other company or person whose negligence caused the injury, and an uninsured employer directly.

faqs.question: What is a redemption, and should I take one?

answer.v: A lump-sum settlement approved by a magistrate that closes the claim, including future medical care. Whether to accept depends on what treatment you will need. Do not sign one without advice.

faqs.question: I reported my injury in Arabic to my supervisor. Does that count?

answer.v: Notice to the employer in any language counts if it was given and understood, but proving it is the problem. Put it in writing in English as well, and keep a copy; we will do it for you.

faqs.question: What does a Dearborn workers’ comp lawyer cost?

answer.v: Nothing up front. Fees are limited by state rule to a percentage of the benefits recovered and must be approved by the magistrate. You owe nothing if no benefits are recovered.
